newsitem.title: USA: Harris says interested in Citicorp futures.
newsitem.headline: Harris says interested in Citicorp futures.

text.p: Harris Futures Corp, a subsidiary of Harris Trust and Savings Bank, would like to acquire Citicorp's futures business, Harris Futures Corp chief executive officer Anthony McCormick said.
"I'd like to do something with them," McCormick said in an interview. "I think it's a great company and I'd like to have the capabilities that they have on the international side."

On Friday, Citicorp said it was reviewing its strategy on its futures business in New York, Chicago, London, Tokyo, and Singapore, and was specifically looking at whether it needs its own execution and clearing functions.
Harris Trust and Savings Bank is owned by Bank of Montreal.
McCormick said he discussed the possibility of acquiring Citicorp's futures business with its U.S. division, Citicorp Futures Corp, but that there had been no follow-up talks.
"We had conceptual discussions, but I can tell you for a fact there is no definitive discussion of it," McCormick said.
Amy Dates, a Citicorp spokeswoman, would not comment on Harris's interest in acquiring Citicorp's futures business.
"We are reviewing a variety of options," Dates said. "But it's impossible to say what the review will culminate in."

McCormick said Harris Futures Corp was attracted to Citicorp's presence on the London International Financial Futures & Options Exchange (LIFFE) and the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX). Citicorp's futures business in Britain is run by Citifutures Ltd.
"We don't have direct presence on either of those markets, so for us that would be very attractive," McCormick said.
"We are probably more concentrated in Chicago than they are, particularly on the customer side," he said. Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
